meta.title: TriggerHub | Automate your stream workflow
meta.description: TriggerHub is a Windows desktop app for streamers. Build trigger-macro automations that connect OBS, Spotify, and your tools and runs locally, no cloud required.
meta.ogDescription: A Windows desktop automation tool for streamers and creators. Connect OBS, Spotify, and your tools in one local workflow hub.

footer.productInfo: TriggerHub is a Windows desktop automation tool for streamers and creators. Currently in early access; the core engine is built, integrations are in active development.

hero.title: Automate your stream. Stay focused live.
hero.description: TriggerHub is a Windows desktop app that connects OBS, Spotify, and your streaming tools through triggers and macros. Automations run locally on your machine, nothing in the cloud between you and your setup.

benefits.title: Less manual work. More time actually streaming.
benefits.description: TriggerHub handles the repetitive parts of your stream setup so you can stay focused on what's in front of the camera.

features.title: Core automation, built for live setups.
features.description: The trigger engine and macro system are already working. OBS and Spotify adapters are in the codebase and actively being improved.

workflow.title: Three steps from event to action.
workflow.description: Every automation in TriggerHub follows the same model: detect an event, apply conditions, run the action locally.

extensions.title: The foundation supports more than the current scope.
extensions.description: Plugin scaffolding, clip modules, and a local runtime are already in the codebase. These are natural next directions, not roadmap promises.

trust.title: Built on real implementation, not mockups.
trust.description: Every claim on this page is backed by code in the repository.

faq.title: Straight answers about TriggerHub.
faq.description: What it is today, what's in development, and what it isn't.

items.title: No more manual switching
items.description: Set up the routine once. When your stream starts, the right scene loads, the music kicks in, and your tools respond without touching anything.

items.title: Runs entirely on your machine
items.description: TriggerHub has no cloud backend for automations. Everything executes locally, delivering low latency, no external dependency, no privacy concerns.

items.title: One workflow system for your whole setup
items.description: Triggers, conditions, macros, and actions share a single workflow model. You manage one context instead of juggling three interfaces.

items.title: Trigger engine
items.description: Define the event that kicks off a workflow. Stream status changes, hotkeys, timed events; the engine picks up the signal and starts execution.
bullets: Condition checks before any action runs

items.title: Macro system
items.description: Group actions into sequences you can reuse across workflows. Run steps in order, in parallel, or conditionally, built once, applied anywhere.

items.title: Service adapters (in development)
items.description: Early adapters for OBS and Spotify are in the codebase. Twitch has polling-based stream status detection. These are actively being hardened, not yet production-stable.
bullets: Clip modules and plugin scaffolding included

items.title: Pick your trigger
items.description: Choose the event that starts the automation, a stream going live, a hotkey, a scene change. That's your entry point.

items.title: Define the logic
items.description: Add conditions to control when the automation should continue. Chain steps into a macro that runs exactly how you configured it.

items.title: Run the action locally
items.description: The automation executes on your machine. OBS switches, Spotify plays, your tools respond with no cloud relay, no added latency.

items.title: Desktop-first, not cloud-first
items.description: TriggerHub runs on your machine. There is no cloud backend in the automation execution path.

items.title: Core modules are shipped
items.description: The trigger engine, macro system, and service adapter scaffolding are in the repository and working.

items.title: Local execution
items.description: Automations don't leave your machine. No keys sent to third parties, no network dependency when an action fires.

items.title: Tested build pipeline
items.description: Automated tests and a production build pipeline cover both the website and the desktop codebase.

items.title: Touch-surface control
items.description: The architecture already points toward a secondary display or tablet control surface. Soundboard-style stream control is a natural extension of the current desktop model.
bullets: Second-screen or tablet operation is a documented target direction
Soundboard workflows are referenced in project docs
Extends the desktop control model; doesn't shift it

items.title: Richer clip workflows
items.description: Clip export modules and a plugin system are already in the codebase. A more capable clip pipeline with auto-save, processing, editor integration follows naturally from there.
bullets: Clip export is already part of the repository scope
Plugin system exists as an extension point
Content tooling improvements are on the roadmap

items.title: AI-assisted post-production
items.description: The roadmap mentions AI-assisted creator workflows as a later direction. A future plugin for clip refinement, tagging, and publishing fits the existing architecture, framed as possible, not current.
bullets: Positioned as a possible extension, not a current feature
Grounded in roadmap notes about AI-assisted workflows
Keeps the product honest while showing where it can go

items.question: What is TriggerHub today?
items.answer: A Windows desktop automation app in early access. The trigger engine and macro system work. OBS and Spotify adapters are in the codebase and being actively developed.

items.question: Which integrations are working right now?
items.answer: OBS and Spotify adapters are in active development. They are present in the codebase but not yet production-stable. Twitch has polling-based stream status detection.

items.question: Is it a cloud product?
items.answer: No. TriggerHub runs entirely on your machine. Automations execute locally, no cloud backend, no external relay.

items.question: Which platform does it support?
items.answer: Windows x64 is the current target. Mac and Linux are not on the near-term roadmap.

cta.title: Get early access.
cta.description: TriggerHub is in active development. Access is limited. Request it to follow the release and get notified when builds are available.
